source_text:
Ἐπεὶ εὐξάμενος θεῷ ἐπέτυχον ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὰ ἀξιόθεα πρόσωπα, ὡς καὶ πλέον ᾐτούμην λαβεῖν: δεδεμένος γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐλπίζω ὑμᾶς ἀσπάσασθαι, ἐάνπερ θέλημα ᾖ τοῦ ἀξιωθῆναί με εἰς τέλος εἶναι.
ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἀρχὴ εὐοικονόμητός ἐστιν, ἐάνπερ χάριτος ἐπιτύχω εἰς τὸ τὸν κλῆρόν μου ἀνεμποδίστως ἀπολαβεῖν. φοβοῦμαι γὰρ τὴν ὑμῶν ἀγάπην, μὴ αὐτή με ἀδικήσῃ. ὑμῖν γὰρ εὐχερές ἐστιν, ὃ θέλετε, ποιῆσαι: ἐμοὶ δὲ δύσκολόν ἐστιν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν, ἐάνπερ ὑμεῖς μὴ φείσησθέ μου.
thought_title: Ignatius fears the Romans' love may hinder his martyrdom
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, writes as a prisoner being taken to Rome, and here he begins his letter to the Roman church by expressing both his joy at the prospect of seeing them and his fear that their love might prevent his martyrdom.
pass_a_gloss: Since, having prayed to God, I succeeded in seeing your faces worthy of God, as indeed I was asking to receive more; for bound in Christ Jesus I hope to greet you, if indeed it be the will for me to be deemed worthy to be at the end. For the beginning is well-ordered, if indeed I obtain grace for the receiving back of my lot without hindrance. For I fear your love, lest it itself wrong me. For for you it is easy to do what you wish; but for me it is difficult to attain God, if indeed you do not spare me.

choices.why: Keeps the adjective's force as a compound of 'worthy' and 'God' without smoothing into a paraphrase; the faces themselves are called worthy of God.
Preserves the dative of sphere and the perfect passive participle's state; 'in Christ Jesus' is the sphere of his binding, not merely the reason.
rejected: a prisoner because of Christ Jesus

choices.english: the receiving back of my lot without hindrance
choices.why: Keeps 'lot' as the metaphor for his appointed destiny (martyrdom) and renders the adverb literally as 'without hindrance' rather than a smoother 'unhindered' to preserve the adverbial force.
rejected: to obtain my portion without obstacle

choices.why: The reflexive 'αὐτή' is emphatic; 'wrong' keeps the legal-moral force of ἀδικέω without importing 'harm' which would soften the sense of injustice.

choices.english: if indeed you do not spare me
choices.why: φείδομαι with genitive means 'spare' in the sense of refraining from intervention; 'spare me' preserves the irony that their mercy would actually hinder him.
rejected: if you do not refrain from me
unless you hold back from me

pass_b_english: I prayed to God, and I have succeeded in seeing your faces, which are worthy of God. I was asking for even more than this. For I am bound in Christ Jesus, and I hope to greet you, if it is God's will that I be deemed worthy to reach the end.

The beginning is well ordered, if indeed I obtain the grace to receive back my lot without hindrance. For I fear your love, lest it wrong me. For it is easy for you to do what you want, but it is difficult for me to attain God, if you do not spare me.

problems.quote: succeeded in seeing your faces worthy of God
problems.source_quote: ἐπέτυχον ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὰ ἀξιόθεα πρόσωπα
problems.why: ἀξιόθεα modifies πρόσωπα, not the seeing; 'faces worthy of God' misattributes the worthiness
problems.fix: succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces

problems.quote: I have received even more than I asked
problems.why: ᾐτούμην is imperfect 'I was asking', not 'I asked'; λαβεῖν is infinitive 'to receive', not 'I have received'
problems.fix: as I was also asking to receive even more
problems.ruling: ὡς καὶ πλέον ᾐτούμην λαβεῖν = 'as I was asking to receive more'; English wrongly makes it a completed past action.

edits.old: succeeded in seeing your faces worthy of God
edits.new: succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces

edits.old: I have received even more than I asked
edits.new: as I was also asking to receive even more

problems.quote: Since I have prayed to God and succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces, as I was also asking to receive even more
problems.why: Tense confusion: 'succeeded' vs. 'was asking'; has he seen them or not?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Since I have prayed to God to succeed in seeing your faces...'

edits.old: Since I have prayed to God and succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces, as I was also asking to receive even more.
edits.new: Since I have prayed to God and have succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces, as I was also asking to receive even more.

fixed: The tense confusion is resolved by adding 'have' before 'succeeded', making clear that the seeing has already happened while the asking was ongoing.

last_rejected.why: ἐπέτυχον means 'obtained' or 'was granted,' not 'succeeded'; God granted the prayer, not Ignatius succeeded.
last_rejected.fix: Since I prayed to God and was granted to see your God-worthy faces
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπέτυχον means 'obtain/grant' or 'succeed in'; 'succeeded in seeing' is within normal range and not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: as I was also asking to receive even more
last_rejected.why: ᾐτούμην is imperfect 'I was asking,' but context shows he asked for more than just seeing them—he asked for even more than this sight.
last_rejected.fix: as I was asking to receive even more than this
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς καὶ πλέον ᾐτούμην λαβεῖν: 'as I was also asking to receive even more' accurately renders the Greek; claim is a preference.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἀρχὴ εὐοικονόμητός ἐστιν
last_rejected.why: εὐοικονόμητος means 'easy to manage' or 'favorable,' not 'well-ordered'; the start is favorable/easy, not orderly.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐοικονόμητος can mean 'well-ordered/well-managed'; rendering is within semantic range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ἀπολαβεῖν here means 'to obtain' or 'receive,' not 'receive back'; no 'back' is implied.
last_rejected.fix: to obtain my lot without hindrance
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπολαβεῖν can mean 'receive back'; with κλῆρόν, 'receiving back my lot' is reasonable, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: it is difficult for me to attain God
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐμοὶ δὲ δύσκολόν ἐστιν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν
last_rejected.why: ἐπιτυχεῖν τοῦ θεοῦ means 'to attain to God' or 'reach God' (final goal), but 'attain God' is awkward and potentially misleading in English; however, 'attain God' is within semantic range. More critically, the phrase means reaching God through martyrdom, which 'attain God' obscures.
last_rejected.fix: but it is hard for me to reach God
last_rejected.ruling: τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιτυχεῖν: 'attain God' is within semantic range; martyrdom context is implicit, not a major mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: if indeed you do not spare me
last_rejected.why: φείδεσθαι means 'spare' in sense of 'refrain from,' but here it means 'hold back from' preventing his martyrdom; 'spare me' misleadingly suggests they might kill him, when they might rescue him.
last_rejected.fix: if you do not hold back from me
last_rejected.ruling: φείσησθέ μου: 'spare me' is standard meaning; context (not rescuing him) is clear from surrounding text, not misleading.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence so the reader understands Ignatius has already seen the Ephesians' faces and was asking for more than that. Broke the long first paragraph into two paragraphs where the thought turns from his hope to greet them to his fear that their love might prevent his martyrdom. Kept every claim and qualification exactly.

notes.quote: Since I have prayed to God and succeeded in seeing your God-worthy faces, as I was also asking to receive even more
notes.why: Tense confusion: 'succeeded' vs. 'was asking'; has he seen them or not?
notes.fix: Clarify: 'Since I have prayed to God to succeed in seeing your faces...'
